newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli minister visits jailed Hamas founder.
newsitem.headline: Israeli minister visits jailed Hamas founder.

text.p: Israel's public security minister on Tuesday visited the jailed spiritual leader of the Islamic militant Hamas movement and said there was room to discuss freeing the ailing clergyman.

Avigdor Kahalani said he wanted to check on the health of the wheelchair-bound Sheikh Ahmed Yassin, jailed by Israel in 1989 for life on charges of founding Hamas. Israel also holds him responsible for the kidnapping and killing of two soldiers.
"I came to see first of all how he feels and if his medical treatment is good," Kahalani told reporters who accompanied him on the visit at the Ramleh Prison hospital in central Israel.
Asked if he supported freeing Yassin, Kahalani said: "There is room to discuss the matter." He did not elaborate.

Yassin, 60, complained to Kahalani that he had not seen some of his 11 children for more than six years because of Israeli restrictions on family visits and demanded he be allowed to join other inmates for Friday prayers.
Yassin's family live in self-ruled Gaza, where most Palestinians are barred from entering Israel unless they receive special permits.
Asked if he wanted to tell Israelis anything, Yassin said: "I want Israel to give the Palestinian people their rights so they can gain freedom and independence."

Hamas, which wants to establish an Islamic state in all of Palestine -- including Israel -- has waged a campaign of suicide bombings against the Jewish state. Yassin and six other men founded the group as an offshoot of the Moslem Brotherhood movement in 1987.
